ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an object moves along a straight line, with points A, B, and C being three points on the line. The object moves at a constant velocity between points A and B. Upon reaching point B, it begins to decelerate uniformly until it comes to a stop at point C. In the 2nd second before stopping, the object covers a distance of 4.5 m while decelerating uniformly. It is known that the distance between points A and C is 60 m, and the total time for the object to travel from A to C is 11 s.

1. The magnitude of the acceleration during the process of an object's deceleration.
2. the distance between B and C

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an object moves along a straight line, with points A, B, and C being three points on the line. The object moves at a constant velocity between points A and B. Upon reaching point B, it begins to decelerate uniformly until it comes to a stop at point C. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal straight line, A is at the left end, B is located toward the right, C is at the right end, and the three points are arranged on the same straight line in the order A, B, C; the problem statement explains that the AB segment is uniform motion, after the object reaches B it uniformly decelerates in the BC segment, and finally stops at point C. Reasoning: Looking at the uniformly decelerated motion in the BC segment in reverse, it is equivalent to the object starting from rest at point C and doing uniformly accelerated motion, with the magnitude of acceleration set as a. The displacement during the 2nd second before stopping is the displacement in the reverse motion from the end of the 1st second to the end of the 2nd second: 4.5 = (1/2)a(2^2 - 1^2). Therefore 4.5 = 1.5a, giving a = 3 m/s^2. Let the deceleration time from B to C be T. The velocity when reaching point B is v_B = aT = 3T, and the BC distance is s_BC = (1/2)aT^2 = 1.5T^2. The time of uniform motion in the AB segment is 11 - T, and the velocity is v_B = 3T, so the AB distance is s_AB = 3T(11 - T). Also, the total AC distance is 60 m, so 3T(11 - T) + 1.5T^2 = 60. Simplifying gives T^2 - 22T + 40 = 0, solving gives T = 2 s or 20 s. Since the total time is only 11 s, discard T = 20 s and take T = 2 s. Thus BC = 1.5 × 2^2 = 6 m.
